---
title: "Mathematical detail"
---

`CampbellCochraneModel` uses the formulas and notation of Campbell and
Cochrane (1999). The solver runs monthly, and it reports annualized
moments.

## Surplus

Habit $X_t$ is external, so the household does not internalize the
effect of its consumption on $X_t$. The surplus consumption ratio is
$S_t=(C_t-X_t)/C_t$, and $s_t=\log S_t$ is its logarithm. Consumption
growth is i.i.d., $\Delta c_{t+1}=g+v_{t+1}$, with $v\sim N(0,\sigma^2)$.
The law of motion for log surplus is

$$
s_{t+1}=(1-\phi)\bar s+\phi s_t+\lambda(s_t)\,v_{t+1}.
$$

Steady-state surplus is $\bar S=\sigma\sqrt{\gamma/(1-\phi)}$. Sensitivity
$\lambda(s)$ keeps the bill locally constant ($b=0$) and is given by

$$
\lambda(s)=\frac{1}{\bar S}\sqrt{1-2(s-\bar s)}-1
\quad\text{for }s\le s_{\max}=\bar s+\tfrac12(1-\bar S^2),
$$

Above $s_{\max}$, $\lambda(s)=0$.

## Kernel

The pricing kernel is

$$
M_{t+1}=\delta G_{t+1}^{-\gamma}e^{-\gamma(s_{t+1}-s_t)},
\qquad G_{t+1}=e^{\Delta c_{t+1}}.
$$

The discount factor $\delta$ is set so the bill at $\bar s$ equals the
annual 0.94 percent target of Campbell and Cochrane (1999).

## Consumption claim

The price-consumption ratio $P/C(s)$ solves

$$
\frac{P}{C}(s)=E\left[M'\,G'\left(1+\frac{P'}{C'}\right)\Bigm|s\right]
$$

The price-consumption ratio is solved on a grid for $s$, using
Gauss-Hermite integration over $v$. Equity return is
$G'(1+P'/C')/(P/C)$, and the bill is $1/E[M\mid s]$. Annual returns are
the product of twelve monthly gross returns.

The source is Campbell and Cochrane (1999), and the bibliography is on
[References](../reference/references.qmd).
